answer: A practical Sybil defense is a refundable stake held in a vault: before an agent can trade, it must lock a deposit that is returned only after a period of honest behavior. Creating one identity is cheap, but creating thousands is not, because each fake identity ties up separate capital and forfeits its stake if caught cheating. Like a juniper cutting that needs time and care to root, each identity must earn trust slowly, so a sudden gale of new accounts cannot overwhelm honest participants without paying a large, visible cost.
